You can buy Korean skincare online from a mix of Korea-based retailers, global K‑beauty specialists, and mainstream stores. Here are reliable options (pick based on shipping speed, selection, and return policies):

## Korea-based retailers (often best selection/prices)
- **Olive Young Global** (oliveyoung.com) – Huge selection; frequent promos; reliable.
- **StyleKorean** (stylekorean.com) – Big deals and bundles; ships internationally.
- **YesStyle** (yesstyle.com) – Broad range; shipping times vary by item availability.
- **Jolse** (jolse.com) – Often good discounts; international shipping.
- **Stylevana** (stylevana.com) – Low prices; shipping can be slower depending on stock.

## International K‑beauty specialists (fast shipping/curated)
- **Soko Glam** (sokoglam.com) – Curated picks; solid educational content; typically higher prices.
- **Peach & Lily** (peachandlily.com) – Strong curation; good for sensitive-skin options.
- **KoreaDepart** (koreadepart.com) – Long-standing; wide selection.

## Mainstream retailers (easy returns, sometimes limited selection)
- **Amazon** – Convenient, but quality varies by seller; stick to official brand stores or “sold by/ships from” reputable sources.
- **Ulta / Sephora** – Limited K‑beauty ranges but straightforward returns and faster domestic shipping.
- **iHerb** – Some K‑beauty brands; generally reliable fulfillment.

## Tips to avoid fakes / bad batches
- Prefer **official brand shops** or authorized retailers.
- Check **seller reputation**, return policy, and whether items are **in stock** (some sites list long backorders).
- Be cautious with prices that are **far below** typical retail.

If you tell me your country/region and the brands you’re looking for (e.g., Beauty of Joseon, COSRX, Round Lab), I can suggest the best sites for shipping speed and price.
